newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber closes down at midday prices.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber closes down at midday prices.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices retained midday levels to close lower after the market drifted through the day without consumer interest, traders said.

At the close, July RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 282 Malaysian/Singapore cents ($1.12) a kg, down half cent from Monday. July SMR20 buyer was quoted 1.50 cents lower at 260.50.
A check with trading houses also showed most of them quoting noon prices, offering the SMR 20 at 259, SMR 10 at 261, SMR 5 at 271, SMR CV at 330, SMR L at 307, and drum latex at 226.
"The market is just stagnant, there's nothing moving," said a trader.
The INRO five-day average ended at 215.45 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on June 9 against 216.06 on June 6. The daily indicator was at 213.86 against 214.32 previously.
A Malaysian-based shipping agent quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $800 per TEU and $1,700 per two-TEU containers.
